title: Arachin daf 8

chapters.title: Hair of an executed woman
chapters.about: Discussion on whether hair extensions are considered part of the body or separate assets.

chapters.title: Comparing human and animal execution
chapters.about: Analyzing the difference between a woman and an animal regarding when they become asur.

chapters.title: Limits of Arachin vows
chapters.about: The minimum and maximum values for vows and how to handle insufficient funds.

chapters.title: Multiple vows and payment priority
chapters.about: Rules for paying off multiple vows when funds are limited.

chapters.title: Nida and Ziva cycles
chapters.about: Background on the Nida and Ziva cycle and how to fix a lost count.

chapters.title: Fixing a lost cycle count
chapters.about: Calculating the number of clean days required based on the number of days bled.

chapters.title: Korbanot for a woman who lost count
chapters.about: When a woman who made a mistake in her cycle brings a Korban.

claims: Rabbi Soffer explores the laws of Arachin, specifically focusing on the valuation of vows and the rules for a woman who has lost track of her Nida and Ziva cycle.
He examines the minimum and maximum limits for valuations and discusses the halakhic requirements for a woman to return to a state of certainty regarding her cycle.
summary: Rabbi Soffer explores the laws of Arachin, specifically focusing on the valuation of vows and the rules for a woman who has lost track of her Nida and Ziva cycle. He examines the minimum and maximum limits for valuations and discusses the halakhic requirements for a woman to return to a state of certainty regarding her cycle.
questions: What are the minimum and maximum amounts for an Arachin vow?
How does a woman who has lost track of her cycle determine when she is tahor?
What happens if a person makes multiple vows but does not have enough funds to cover all of them?
Why is a woman's hair considered mutar after she is executed?
When is a Korban brought by a woman who has lost track of her cycle?
